tickets.background:
Phase P0 Crate Foundation & Scope Definition covers the crate purpose (N0001-related), non-goals and Tauri integration boundary (N0003), terminology glossary (N0004), compliance requirements including MSRV/OS targets (N0005), versioning policy (N0006), 15-item normative functional requirements scope (N0007), module directory structure and crate responsibility rationale (N0008), and M20 implementation priority map with design decision table (N0002). These 7 nodes form the foundational specification that constrains all downstream implementation phases.

### Goal
Produce a single authoritative spec document (`specs/P0-1.md`) that defines siprs crate identity, design constraints, and implementation roadmap. The spec must consolidate 7 RFC architectural nodes into a coherent, internally consistent specification that serves as the reference for all downstream implementation tickets (P0-2 through P0-6, and all P1+ phases). Every downstream ticket must be traceable back to a section in this foundation spec.

### Purpose
The siprs crate cannot be implemented piecemeal without a shared understanding of what the crate IS and IS NOT. Without an explicit foundation specification, each implementation ticket would operate with its own implicit assumptions about crate scope, module layout, naming conventions, and architectural boundaries — leading to integration failures, duplicated effort, and design drift. This spec establishes the common ground: a single source of truth for crate purpose, non-goals, terminology, compliance constraints, functional requirements, module structure, versioning, and implementation priority.

### Motivation
Current codebase has partial implementations scattered across `src/` sub-directories (api/, build/, config/, error/, model/, security/, state/, tests/) — these grew organically from boundify-graph output without an overarching spec. New contributors (including AI agents) lack a unified reference for what the crate should ultimately become. The RFC-ROOT.md contains comprehensive design but in prose form, not as a structured implementation spec. Creating P0-1 spec closes the gap between the RFC design intent and the scattered implementation artifacts, providing a structured foundation for the TDD workflow in all subsequent tickets.

### Constraints
- **Time**: This ticket produces a spec document only — no executable Rust code. Spec must be created before any implementation ticket enters the Green phase.
- **Scope boundary**: Spec covers only N0001–N0008 nodes. Downstream nodes (N0009 concurrency, N0010 command serialization, N0011 public API, N0013 ClientConfig, N0033 AudioMixer, N0037 FFI layer, N0039 build strategy, N0043 shutdown, N0045 lock rules, N0046 observability, N0047 security, N0050 audio device, N0052 test strategy, N0055 panic policy, N0057 acceptance criteria) are referenced only as forward pointers, not fully specified.
- **Consistency constraint**: Spec must not contradict any existing implementation in `src/` without a note documenting the deviation. Existing `src/config/versioning_policy.rs` must be referenced accurately.

tickets.background:
## Goal
Establish the single-core-reactor concurrency foundation for the siprs crate. The runtime/ module delivers a dedicated reactor thread that serializes all PJSUA control API calls through an unbounded MPSC channel, achieving Send+Sync safety without exposing PJSUA thread-safety constraints to library users.

## Purpose
PJSIP internally spawns native threads and fires callbacks on arbitrary threads. Calling pjsua_* functions from multiple threads concurrently causes data races, undefined behavior, and panics. This ticket implements the CoreReactor thread that owns the single source of truth (ClientState) and processes all commands sequentially.

## Motivation
Every higher-level feature (accounts, calls, audio, events) depends on thread-safe access to PJSIP. Without this foundation, the crate cannot provide any safe public API. The MPSC+oneshot pattern is the architectural invariant that unlocks all downstream tickets (P0-3 through P1+).

## Constraints
- Single-core-reactor: exactly one std::thread::JoinHandle<()> for all PJSUA control
- RuntimeCommand uses tokio::sync::mpsc::UnboundedSender for submission (never bounded channels - must not deadlock on backpressure)
- Each command variant carries a tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<Result<_, SipError>> for async reply
- Four execution contexts explicitly modeled but only #1 (User async) and #2 (Core reactor) are instantiated in P0-2; #3 (PJSIP callbacks, P0-6) and #4 (Audio worker, P1+) are interface contracts only
- Lock rules: read().await for query snapshot APIs; write().await for reactor state mutation; blocking_read() prohibited
- ClientState source of truth is owned exclusively by reactor thread, not by RwLock - RwLock is only for snapshot sharing
- conf_port_id lives in PjsuaBackend, not in CallEntry

## Investigation Results

### RFC Graph Analysis
- **N0009 (Section 7 Concurrency Model & Execution Contexts)**: Defines 4 execution contexts, single-reactor architecture, MPSC command serialization. Key design decisions: (1) PJSIP callbacks must NOT call pjsua_* directly - only enqueue work, (2) Audio worker tasks communicate via lock-free queue, (3) Single reactor sufficient for ~30 concurrent calls.
- **N0010 (Section 7.2 RuntimeCommand & Command Serialization)**: Full RuntimeCommand enum with 10 variants, each carrying oneshot::Sender for async reply. Enum design ensures all pjsua_* calls go through the channel, guaranteeing Send+Sync.
- **N0045 (Section 33 Runtime Internal State & Lock Rules)**: ClientState/AccountEntry/CallEntry struct definitions. Lock rules: read().await for queries (blocking_read() prohibited - will panic inside tokio runtime), write().await for reactor updates. conf_port_id managed by PjsuaBackend, not exposed in CallEntry.

### Existing Code Analysis
- `src/lib.rs` lines 44: `// [::STUB::] P0-2: runtime/ - Reactor, Command, Handle` - module is declared but commented out. Need to uncomment.
- `src/concurrency_contexts/command_serialization.rs` - contains `pub trait Service {}` stub bound to N0010. This is a DIFFERENT design approach (trait-based) from the enum-based RFC section 7.2. P0-2 implements the enum-based design. The Service trait should remain as a [::STUB::] cross-reference.
- `src/error/error_design_siperror.rs` - SipError is a stub `pub enum Error {}` (P0-4). P0-2 needs its own internal error type.
- `src/error/m20_runtime_command_error.rs` - N0017: RuntimeCommand error design stub (P0-4 M20 refinement).
- `src/error/m20_shutdown_routing.rs` - N0044: M20 Shutdown command routing stub (P1).
- `src/model/id_design_newtype.rs` - AccountId/CallId stubs (P0-3). P0-2 uses u64 placeholders.
- `Cargo.toml` - tokio with sync/rt/rt-multi-thread/time/macros features already present. No new crate deps needed.

### Key Architectural Decisions
1. **Enum dispatch rather than trait dispatch**: RFC section 7.2 specifies a concrete RuntimeCommand enum with named variants. This is intentional - it enables exhaustive match in the reactor loop and compile-time verification that every command is handled.
2. **Unbounded MPSC (not bounded)**: PJSIP operations can have unpredictable completion times; a bounded channel would risk deadlock under load. Memory is bounded by the rate of command submission from the single user async context.
3. **reactor thread is not equal to tokio runtime thread**: The reactor runs on a dedicated std::thread (non-tokio) to avoid blocking the async runtime with synchronous pjsua_* calls. The reactor can block; tokio tasks must not.
4. **ClientState ownership**: Single-writer (reactor) + multiple-reader (async queries) pattern via tokio::sync::RwLock. The RwLock guards the SNAPSHOT, not the source of truth - the source of truth is the reactor thread's local state variable.

tickets.background:
### Goal
Establish the siprs crate's public identity as a safe asynchronous SIP audio client library. Define SipClient as the top-level facade that integrates with P0-2's CoreReactor/RuntimeHandle/RuntimeCommand infrastructure.

### Purpose
Provide Rust application code with a safe, async-native facade over PJSUA SIP functionality, limited to audio-only voice communication. This crate exists to eliminate unsafe FFI boilerplate and deliver SIP calling capabilities through idiomatic Rust APIs — Result propagation, tokio async/await, typed events, and structured configuration.

### Motivation
P0-3 is the gateway ticket that establishes the crate's architectural identity before downstream tickets implement specific sub-systems: error types (P0-4), event system (P0-5), FFI layer (P0-6), audio pipeline (P1+). Without a defined SipClient + ClientConfig, no downstream implementation has a cohesive host. This ticket crystallizes the purpose defined in RFC 1 (§1) into concrete public API surface.

### Constraints
- Audio-only: no video API surface (RFC §1, §2). Enforced by compile-time assertions.
- All async public APIs must return Result<T, SipError> (RFC §1 constraint on N0001).
- PJSIP v2.x via FFI only — no raw socket-level SIP stack.
- Single crate with modular internal structure (RFC §6, C009).
- Shutdown must be cancellation-safe and idempotent (RFC §32, C044).
- SecretString for password storage (RFC §35-36, C048).
- Microphone input is optional via cpal-input feature flag (RFC §40, C051).
- MSRV 1.95, OS targets per RFC §4 (C006).

scope: DtmfMethod: Inband, SipInfo, Rfc4733 for send and receive
DtmfReceivedInfo: method, digit, duration_ms, volume_dbm0
DTMF policy validation: send_dtmf rejects methods not in account policy
AsyncAudioSource trait with async fn next_chunk via RPITIT
ErasedAudioSource automatic derivation for dynamic dispatch
SyncAudioSource trait and SyncSourceAdapter
IncomingCall struct: from_uri, to_uri, display_name, headers, offered_codecs, has_early_media
Optional auto-reject timer for unanswered incoming calls
ReferRequest: refer_to, referred_by, replaces
Blind transfer with NOTIFY-based completion
testUnit: UT: DtmfMethod validation against account policy
UT: AsyncAudioSource next_chunk fills buffer correctly
UT: SyncSourceAdapter wraps synchronous source into async trait

phases.summary:
P7 implements Raw SIP message specification (redact/headers), call control API (answer/hangup/hold/transfer/send_dtmf), audio subscribe API with AudioTapMode (Realtime/Lossless) and backpressure policy, and SubscribeAudio Reactor handler with MediaDirection and conf_connect.
---
P8 implements DTMF specification (DtmfMethod, DtmfReceived/DtmfSent), AsyncAudioSource trait with RPITIT and dynamic dispatch, SyncSourceAdapter, incoming call handling with auto-reject timer, and REFER/blind transfer protocol.
